messages.text: How do changes in automotive radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Vector Network Analyzer?

【推論】For the automotive-radar cases described, moving to 76 GHz to 81 GHz operation, multi-GHz instantaneous bandwidth, dynamic artificial objects, angular directions and Doppler means the VNA needs higher mmWave frequency coverage, wider swept spans, time-domain capability, group-delay/amplitude-flatness measurement, and higher dynamic range.[28][30][26][25][2][27]
The passages list automotive radar RF bands of 24 GHz to 24.25 GHz and 76 GHz to 81 GHz, while QAT100 with AREG800A supports 76 GHz to 77 GHz and 77 GHz to 81 GHz with 4 GHz RF instantaneous bandwidth.[30][28]
【推論】If direct RF-path VNA measurement is needed for 76 GHz to 81 GHz radar hardware, a 67 GHz base VNA does not cover the full band, while a 10 MHz to 110 GHz ZNA67EXT VNA system does.[15][21][28]
The AREG800A IF side expands to 1 GHz, 2 GHz or 5 GHz instantaneous IF bandwidth, with IF frequency ranges listed as 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz.[30]
VNA measurement conditions for AREG800A IF transfer characteristics require 2.5 MHz frequency step size, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power and spans matching 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz or 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz.[3]
Suppression of ghost objects is measured with a vector network analyzer in time domain, using 125 kHz frequency step size, 100 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power and the same IF-span families.[2]
RF transfer-characteristic measurements for AREG8-81S / AREG8-81D use 2.5 MHz frequency step size, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, a Hann normal gate and bandpass filter from RX waveguide input to TX waveguide output.[27]
Those RF transfer-characteristic measurements include amplitude flatness over 1 GHz, 2 GHz and 4 GHz bandwidths and group-delay flatness over 1 GHz, 2 GHz and 4 GHz bandwidths.[27]
The AREG800A supports dynamic artificial object generation, with hybrid analog/digital echo generation to 3000 m or digital FMCW echo generation to 3000 m.[26]
The AREG800A also supports individual Doppler frequency shift per artificial object, ±500 km/h velocity setting range and 0.001 km/h velocity step size with AREG8-B9 and AREG8-B63.[25]
The AREG800A dynamic RCS range is 90 dB for all artificial objects on one IF path with listed mmWave frontends and 60 dB for multiple objects per IF path with those frontends.[3]
【推論】Because the radar echo tests specify ghost suppression, dynamic RCS range and multi-object behavior, VNA dynamic range and sensitivity become important measurement capabilities; the ZNA series lists dynamic range above 129 dB without options, 147 dB typical with options and up to 170 dB maximum attainable range.[2][3][7]
For the 75 GHz to 80 GHz and 80 GHz to 90 GHz regions, the ZNA67EXT dynamic range is specified as above 100 dB and above 105 dB respectively at 10 Hz measurement bandwidth without user correction.[55]
The ZNA series also supports time domain analysis as software options and supports mmWave converter setups, while its 4-port architecture provides true parallel and coherent data acquisition for antenna array tests and antenna test systems.[42][37][38]

【推論】For the automotive-radar cases described, moving to 76 GHz to 81 GHz operation, multi-GHz instantaneous bandwidth, dynamic artificial objects, angular directions and Doppler means the VNA needs higher mmWave frequency coverage, wider swept spans, time-domain capability, group-delay/amplitude-flatness measurement, and higher dynamic range.[28][30][26][25][2][27]
The passages list automotive radar RF bands of 24 GHz to 24.25 GHz and 76 GHz to 81 GHz, while QAT100 with AREG800A supports 76 GHz to 77 GHz and 77 GHz to 81 GHz with 4 GHz RF instantaneous bandwidth.[30][28]
【推論】If direct RF-path VNA measurement is needed for 76 GHz to 81 GHz radar hardware, a 67 GHz base VNA does not cover the full band, while a 10 MHz to 110 GHz ZNA67EXT VNA system does.[15][21][28]
The AREG800A IF side expands to 1 GHz, 2 GHz or 5 GHz instantaneous IF bandwidth, with IF frequency ranges listed as 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz.[30]
VNA measurement conditions for AREG800A IF transfer characteristics require 2.5 MHz frequency step size, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power and spans matching 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz or 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz.[3]
Suppression of ghost objects is measured with a vector network analyzer in time domain, using 125 kHz frequency step size, 100 kHz measurement bandwidth, –10 dBm source power and the same IF-span families.[2]
RF transfer-characteristic measurements for AREG8-81S / AREG8-81D use 2.5 MHz frequency step size, 1 kHz measurement bandwidth, a Hann normal gate and bandpass filter from RX waveguide input to TX waveguide output.[27]
Those RF transfer-characteristic measurements include amplitude flatness over 1 GHz, 2 GHz and 4 GHz bandwidths and group-delay flatness over 1 GHz, 2 GHz and 4 GHz bandwidths.[27]
The AREG800A supports dynamic artificial object generation, with hybrid analog/digital echo generation to 3000 m or digital FMCW echo generation to 3000 m.[26]
The AREG800A also supports individual Doppler frequency shift per artificial object, ±500 km/h velocity setting range and 0.001 km/h velocity step size with AREG8-B9 and AREG8-B63.[25]
The AREG800A dynamic RCS range is 90 dB for all artificial objects on one IF path with listed mmWave frontends and 60 dB for multiple objects per IF path with those frontends.[3]
【推論】Because the radar echo tests specify ghost suppression, dynamic RCS range and multi-object behavior, VNA dynamic range and sensitivity become important measurement capabilities; the ZNA series lists dynamic range above 129 dB without options, 147 dB typical with options and up to 170 dB maximum attainable range.[2][3][7]
For the 75 GHz to 80 GHz and 80 GHz to 90 GHz regions, the ZNA67EXT dynamic range is specified as above 100 dB and above 105 dB respectively at 10 Hz measurement bandwidth without user correction.[55]
The ZNA series also supports time domain analysis as software options and supports mmWave converter setups, while its 4-port architecture provides true parallel and coherent data acquisition for antenna array tests and antenna test systems.[42][37][38]
